subcommittees.name: Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Affects Coast Guard members, operational personnel, and individuals subject to maritime controlled substance laws.
dimensions.evidence: The bill directs the Coast Guard to update its policy regarding the use of medication to treat drug overdoses to require naloxone or a similar medication to be made available to members on all Coast Guard installations

dimensions.assessment: Improves access to emergency overdose medication and broadens the reach of vessel drug laws, impacting emergency response and law enforcement actions.
dimensions.evidence: require naloxone or a similar medication to be made available to members on all Coast Guard installations and in each operational environment.

dimensions.assessment: Requires operational updates and tracking system participation by the Coast Guard without detailing specific separate appropriations.
Amends federal maritime drug statutes and requires administrative policy updates, interagency agreements, and congressional briefings.
dimensions.evidence: Section 70503(a) of title 46, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent policy requirements and tracking mechanisms for Coast Guard operations.

missing_information: Cost estimates for purchasing and stocking naloxone across all Coast Guard installations.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill requires the Coast Guard to update its overdose medication policies, make naloxone available at all facilities and operational environments, participate in a DoD tracking system, and report to Congress. It also clarifies vessel-related controlled substance laws.

card.summary: S. 1071, titled the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and designated as Public Law No. 119-60, establishes the policies, authorizations, and funding levels for U.S. national defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence activities, and maritime and Coast Guard operations. The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.
